title: Off-Board Technologies/MMOTA Software Test Engineer
description:
Job Summary:

  • As an Off-Board Technologies/MMOTA Software Test Engineer, you will be a critical part of a team dedicated to ensuring the highest quality and reliability of vehicle software update pipelines.
  • Your primary focus will be on the end-to-end testing of Over-The-Air (OTA), Service, Human-Machine Interface (HMI), Mobile Apps, and Manufacturing software update processes.
  • You will rigorously test the download, installation, and activation stages to guarantee that all software binaries and configurations are applied precisely as intended, contributing to a best-in-class infotainment system and seamless customer experience.

Responsibilities:
  • Develop and execute comprehensive functional test scenarios and test cases, leveraging user stories within Agile Sprints.
  • Collaborate closely with development teams to understand testing requirements and ensure all project requirements are clearly defined and testable.
  • Prepare, configure, and maintain necessary test benches, vehicles, tools, and software environments to facilitate thorough test execution.
  • Log all test results (pass/fail) following the merge of related test codes into Master, and meticulously debug any failures to ascertain their root cause, ensuring that only valid defects are accurately entered into the defect tracking system, JIRA.
  • Work in conjunction with feature engineers to efficiently reproduce and troubleshoot defects identified within the system.
  • Actively participate in root-cause analysis for both hardware quality problems and software defects.
  • Contribute to system design discussions, documentation efforts, and overall testing strategy to deliver a robust and high-quality infotainment system.
  • Provide accurate time estimates for testing-related tasks during sprint planning sessions to support effective project scheduling.
  • Perform corrective and predictive maintenance on hardware laboratory nodes to ensure they remain in satisfactory condition and functionality for continuous testing.
  • Analyze the root cause of software failures to correctly prioritize them for subsequent fixing, providing timely validation rounds for both manual and automated tests.
  • Contribute to the enhancement of test automation development, optimizing existing processes, validating new features, and supporting testing efforts for upcoming vehicle programs.
  • Identify and propose areas for continuous improvement across all facets of testing and velocity tracking.
  • Utilize Test Management tools for test planning review, execution, monitoring (including proficient key metrics interpretation), and comprehensive reporting of test results.
  • Provide detailed feedback and comprehensive bug reports to foster high-quality software delivery and efficient testing workflows.
  • Successful delivery in Vehicle Software Update pipelines (OTA, Service, HMI, Mobile Apps, and Manufacturing) with software binaries and configurations applied as intended.
  • Key performance indicators demonstrating successful completion of testing and validation for software releases.
  • Comprehensive Test Plans, Test Status, and Defect Reports.
  • Contributions to technical documentation (e.g., design documents, user guides, API documentation, integration guides).
  • User support documentation and training materials as needed.
  • Input into project roadmaps and sprint plans.
  • Maintain functional bench setups and execution of vehicle updates
  • Acceptance Testing - Perform end-to-end acceptance testing on a test vehicle after an OTA update, verifying that all features function as specified in the user stories and meet the defined customer experience criteria for the infotainment system.
  • Test Equipment - Prepare and maintain a hardware test bench, in-vehicle test setup including specific vehicle ECUs and communication modules, to accurately simulate real-world conditions for rigorous testing of OTA software update downloads and installations.
  • Test Automation - Develop and enhance automated test scripts using programming languages (e.g., Python) to validate the successful download, integrity check, and installation of OTA software binaries on simulated vehicle environments within the continuous integration pipeline.
  • Testing - Test - Rigorously execute defined functional test cases for a new manufacturing software update, meticulously documenting all steps and observations to ensure the update process correctly flashes the vehicle's infotainment system and applies configurations as intended.
  • Software Testing - Conduct comprehensive software testing on a new mobile application release designed to initiate vehicle software updates, verifying its functionality across various operating systems and network conditions to ensure reliable update scheduling and status reporting.
  • Testing - Tools - Utilize JIRA to log a newly discovered defect related to an HMI software update failing to install, providing detailed reproduction steps, logs, and screenshots, and then track its resolution through the development lifecycle.
  • Test Execution - Execute a suite of manual and automated test cases on a physical vehicle to validate the successful activation of a newly installed OTA software update, confirming all new features are operational and no regressions have been introduced.
  • Test Integration Testing - Perform integration testing to ensure seamless communication and data flow between the cloud-based OTA update server, the vehicle's telematics unit, and the HMI system during a software update, verifying the entire end-to-end pipeline functions cohesively.
  • Test Cases, Analytical - Analyze user stories and system design specifications for a new infotainment feature to design comprehensive and analytical functional test cases, including edge cases and negative scenarios, to ensure all aspects of the feature's behavior are thoroughly validated post-software update.
  • Test Planning - Develop a detailed test plan for the next sprint's OTA software update, outlining test scope, resources, entry/exit criteria, and estimated timelines for manual and automated testing activities, collaborating closely with the development team.
  • Test Unit Testing - Collaborate with development teams to understand the scope and coverage of unit tests for critical modules within the OTA update client, ensuring individual components correctly handle binary integrity checks and configuration parsing before system-level testing.
  • User Acceptance Testing - Facilitate User Acceptance Testing (UAT) sessions with internal stakeholders or representative customers to gather feedback and confirm that a newly updated HMI interface meets their usability expectations and functional requirements for vehicle control and infotainment.
  • Test Regression Testing - After a critical bug fix is implemented in the OTA update pipeline, execute a full regression test suite covering all previously validated download, installation, and activation scenarios to confirm no existing functionality has been inadvertently broken by the change.
  • Technical Writing - Document the detailed steps and configurations required to set up a new test bench environment for OTA software updates, ensuring clarity and precision for other engineers to replicate the setup accurately.
  • API - Utilize an API testing tool (e.g., Postman) to validate the responses and data structures of the backend APIs responsible for managing vehicle software update campaigns, ensuring that the correct binaries and configurations are being delivered to the vehicles.
  • Python - Write a Python script to automate the parsing of vehicle diagnostic logs and testing data after an OTA update failure.
  • Code Assessment - Review a new piece of software code developed for an infotainment feature, providing feedback to the development team on potential areas that could lead to testing challenges or impact testability, such as missing error handling or complex logic.
  • Automated Scripting - Develop and maintain automated scripts using a scripting language (e.g., Python) to perform repetitive tasks like flashing vehicle ECUs with new software builds, collecting system logs, or initiating and monitoring automated test sequences on a test fleet.

Requirements:
  • 1-5 years of experience in software testing, preferably within embedded systems, automotive, or similar complex software environments.
  • Proven experience in developing and executing functional test scenarios and test cases.
  • Familiarity with Agile development methodologies and working with user stories.
  • Hands-on experience with defect tracking systems (e.g., JIRA) and test management tools.
  • Demonstrated ability to perform root-cause analysis and debug software failures

Education:
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related technical field.

Additional Information:
  • Hybrid - 3-4 days a week onsite/in-vehicle at parking lots/decks/sites

title: Project/Program Manager 5
description:
Scope of Work (SOW)
Implementation of Fully Integrated Vehicle Program Timeline
1. Project Overview
The objective of this engagement is to implement a fully integrated Vehicle Program timeline management system using Primavera P6 or a comparable project management tool. The system will enable seamless integration and visibility across multiple workstreams, including Design, Engineering, Operations, and Enterprise functions. The timeline tool will support detailed planning, scheduling, resource management, and reporting across the Vehicle Program lifecycle.
________________________________________
2. Scope Description
2.1 Core Deliverable
• Deployment and configuration of a centralized, integrated project timeline tool (Primavera P6 or equivalent).
• Integration of key Vehicle Program workstreams: Design, Engineering, Operations, and Enterprise functions.
• Development of customized dashboards and reporting aligned with stakeholder requirements.
• Training and knowledge transfer for internal teams.
2.2 Workstreams Covered
• Design: Concept development, design iterations, approvals.
• Engineering: Detailed engineering schedules, testing, validation, and changes.
• Operations: Manufacturing readiness, supply chain, logistics, and operational milestones.
• Enterprise Functions: Budgeting, resource allocation, risk management, and executive reporting.
________________________________________
3. Project Phases & Timeline
Phase 1: Pilot Implementation (Due by October 31, 2025)
• Setup of Primavera P6 environment tailored for Vehicle Program use.
• Integration of a limited scope pilot covering critical path through Design, Engineering and manufacturing workstreams.
• Development of initial workflows, milestone definitions, and resource allocation parameters.
• Validation of timeline data accuracy and integration points with other systems.
• Delivery of pilot-ready timeline and walkthrough with key stakeholders.
• Initial training session for pilot users.
Phase 2: Full Workstream Integration (Nov 2025 – Feb 2026)
• Expand integration to include full Design, Engineering, Operations, and Enterprise workstreams.
• Consolidation of all program schedules into one master timeline.
• Customization of dashboards and reports for cross-functional visibility.
• Implementation of collaboration and update workflows between teams.
• Ongoing training sessions and documentation updates.
Phase 3: Optimization & Rollout (Mar 2026 – May 2026)
• System optimization based on user feedback and performance metrics.
• Finalization of integration points with other enterprise tools (e.g., ERP, PLM).
• Full rollout across all Vehicle Program teams and stakeholders.
• Comprehensive training program and support materials delivered.
• Establishment of ongoing maintenance and support framework.
________________________________________
4. Vendor Responsibilities
• Provision of all necessary software licenses, if applicable.
• Configuration and customization of Primavera P6 or equivalent tool.
• Integration planning and execution across all designated workstreams.
• Regular progress reporting and status meetings with the Lucid project team.
• Conducting workshops and training sessions.
• Providing detailed documentation, including configuration, workflows, and user manuals.
• Post-implementation support for at least 3 months after full rollout.
________________________________________
5. Lucid Responsibilities
• Provide access to current program data, systems, and subject matter experts.
• Facilitate coordination across internal teams and stakeholders.
• Review and approve deliverables within agreed timelines.
• Provide feedback during pilot and subsequent phases.
________________________________________
6. Success Criteria
• Pilot timeline implemented and validated by Oct 31, 2025.
• Full integration and consolidated timeline available by Feb 2026.
• End-to-end solution operational with trained users and documented workflows by May 2026.
• Positive user feedback and demonstrated improvements in program visibility and coordination.
________________________________________
7. Assumptions & Constraints
• Vendor will have appropriate access to Lucid systems and data.
• Lucid internal resources will be available for collaboration and reviews.
• Any changes in scope beyond initial agreement will be handled via formal change requests.


Detailed Timeline and Workstream Deliverables
________________________________________
Phase 1: Pilot Implementation (By October 31, 2025)
Objective:
Deliver a working pilot timeline integrating critical path through Design, Engineering and manufacturing workstreams.
Workstream Deliverables Key Activities Due Date
Design - Pilot schedule for initial design milestones (concept, reviews, approvals)
- Defined tasks, durations, dependencies - Gather design milestones and task info
- Map tasks into Primavera P6
- Validate dependencies and constraints October 10, 2025
Engineering - Pilot schedule for key engineering tasks (detailed design, testing phases)
- Integration points with Design pilot schedule - Collect engineering task data
- Setup preliminary resource allocation
- Align timelines with Design pilot October 15, 2025
Operations - Identify key manufacturing readiness milestones (for pilot visibility only) - Initial operations milestone definitions October 20, 2025
Enterprise - Define key enterprise reporting metrics and requirements for pilot phase - Develop initial dashboard templates for pilot October 25, 2025
Overall - Primavera P6 pilot environment setup and configuration
- Validation workshop with stakeholders
- Training session for pilot users - Tool configuration
- Data import
- Pilot review meeting October 31, 2025
________________________________________
Phase 2: Full Workstream Integration (Nov 2025 – Feb 2026)
Objective:
Expand and integrate Design, Engineering, Operations, and Enterprise workstreams fully, consolidate timelines, and implement collaboration workflows.
Workstream Deliverables Key Activities Due Date
Design - Full design schedule including all phases and review cycles
- Updated dependencies and resource plans - Complete design task mapping
- Resource leveling and conflict resolution December 15, 2025
Engineering - Complete engineering schedule with detailed testing and validation tasks
- Integrated with Design and Operations - Engineering resource planning
- Risk and issue tracking integration December 30, 2025
Operations - Comprehensive operations schedule (manufacturing, supply chain, logistics)
- Linkages with Engineering milestones - Data gathering from operations teams
- Setup critical path and lead times January 15, 2026
Enterprise - Enterprise functions timeline (budgeting, resource management, risk)
- Custom dashboards and executive reports - Configure KPIs and reporting metrics
- Integrate data sources for real-time reporting January 31, 2026
Overall - Master integrated Vehicle Program timeline
- Cross-workstream collaboration workflows
- User training and documentation updates - Finalize workflows
- User acceptance testing (UAT)
- Training sessions February 28, 2026
________________________________________
Phase 3: Optimization & Rollout (Mar 2026 – May 2026)
Objective:
Optimize system based on feedback, complete integration with enterprise tools, and perform full rollout with training and support.
Workstream Deliverables Key Activities Due Date
Design - Post-rollout support and fine-tuning based on user feedback - Collect feedback and refine design workflows March 31, 2026
Engineering - Integration with other engineering systems (e.g., PLM)
- Final performance tuning - API/configuration for data sync
- Optimize resource usage April 15, 2026
Operations - ERP and supply chain system integration
- Finalized operations timeline visibility - Test integration points
- Update milestone alerts April 30, 2026
Enterprise - Finalized dashboards and executive reports
- Rollout training materials and sessions - Create knowledge base and FAQs
- Conduct train-the-trainer workshops May 15, 2026
Overall - Full program-wide rollout
- Ongoing maintenance and support plan established - Go-live support
- Transition to client support team May 31, 2026


Training Plan for Vehicle Program Timeline Implementation
________________________________________
Training Objectives
• Equip users with necessary skills to use Primavera P6 for program scheduling, tracking, and reporting.
• Enable effective collaboration across Design, Engineering, Operations, and Enterprise teams.
• Ensure smooth transition from legacy processes to integrated timeline management.
• Provide ongoing support and knowledge reinforcement.
________________________________________
Training Overview by Phase
Phase 1: Pilot Training (October 2025)
Audience:
• Core Design, Engineering, Manufacturing and Program Management pilot users (Project schedulers, planners, leads)
Goals:
• Introduce Primavera P6 environment setup for pilot use
• Demonstrate entry and management of design, engineering and manufacturing tasks
• Familiarize users with pilot-specific workflows and reporting dashboards
Format & Duration:

• Hands-on exercises using pilot data
• Q&A session
Materials:

• FAQ document
Follow-up:
• Weekly office hours for 1 month post-training for troubleshooting and support
________________________________________
Phase 2: Full Workstream Training (Dec 2025 – Feb 2026)
Audience:
• All Design, Engineering, Operations, and Enterprise functional users
• Project managers and program coordinators
Goals:
• Comprehensive training on Primavera P6 full functionality
• Task scheduling, resource allocation, dependencies, and risk tracking
• Using dashboards and reports tailored to each workstream
• Collaboration and update workflows between teams
Format & Duration:
• Series of modular training sessions (3 sessions, 2-3 hours each)
• Separate tracks for each workstream + combined session for cross-functional collaboration
• Hands-on practice and scenario walkthroughs
Materials:
• Full User Manual
• Workstream-specific quick reference sheets
• Video tutorials covering core functionalities
• Troubleshooting guide
Follow-up:
• Bi-weekly drop-in sessions for 2 months
• Dedicated support channel (email/slack) for user queries
________________________________________
Phase 3: Optimization & Rollout Training (Mar – May 2026)
Audience:
• All program users including new hires
• Training champions and super-users within each team
Goals:
• Reinforce best practices and advanced features
• Train-the-trainer sessions for internal champions
• Review and update of workflows based on feedback
• Introduce integration with other enterprise systems (ERP, PLM)
Format & Duration:
• Train-the-Trainer workshops (2 full days)
• Refresher webinars (1 hour each) covering advanced topics and new features
• On-demand training videos and e-learning modules
Materials:
• Champion Training Guide
• Updated training video library
• Integration user guides
• Knowledge base articles and FAQs
Follow-up:
• Monthly check-ins with champions for 3 months post-rollout
• Ongoing refresher courses available on demand
________________________________________
Training Success Metrics
• User attendance and participation rates
• Completion rates of hands-on exercises and quizzes
• Feedback surveys measuring confidence and usability
• Reduction in support tickets related to timeline tool usage

title: Technician/Technologist - Testing & Calibration

Job Description:

  • To ensure that when the tool (mold) is moved from one manufacturing location to another, the receiving plant can consistently and reliably produce parts to the exact same specifications as the original plant.

Responsibilities:
  • Process validation: The QE validates the injection molding process at the new facility. This ensures that a robust and repeatable process can be established, documented, and controlled.
  • Dimensional analysis: This role ensures that dimensional layout of initial samples produced at the new location are to print. They compare these measurements to the original PPAP data to confirm dimensional equivalence.
  • Customer PPAP package preparation: They are responsible for collecting PPAP data for the tool transfer. The final package, often at AIAG Level 3 for automotive suppliers, includes:
  • Audit of Process Flow Diagrams (PFD)
  • Audit of Process Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (PFMEA)
  • Audit of Control Plans specific to the receiving facility
  • Measurement System Analysis (MSA)
  • Revision of Dimensional results from the trial run
  • Root cause analysis: The engineer must have knowledge of root cause detection for potential quality issues that arise during the transfer and validation process, using problem-solving tools like the 8D process.
  • Cross-functional collaboration: They work closely with project managers, tooling engineers, process engineers, and the original supplier to ensure a smooth transition with minimal disruption to the supply chain.
  • Customer liaison: For external transfers, the QE acts as the primary quality point of contact for the customer, providing updates and submitting the re-PPAP package for final approval.
Qualifications:
  • Experience: A minimum of 3 to 5 years of related experience in an automotive manufacturing environment, particularly in a tooling or process engineering capacity.
  • Technical expertise: Strong understanding of injection molding, or other relevant manufacturing processes. Experience with Quality Systems like APQP and PPAP is essential for automotive production.
